title: Mexican Trails
subtitle: A Record of Travel in Mexico, 1904–07, and a Glimpse at the Life of the Mexican Indian
summary: An American writer’s record of three years, 1904 to 1907, spent wandering in Mexico on foot, on horseback, and by train, with the photographs he took. He begins with the plateau, Mexico City, and Tacubaya, then lives for a time in Cuernavaca and walks and rides through the villages of Morelos, with visits to Tepoztlán and the ruins of Xochicalco. Later chapters take him to Taxco, Puebla, Cholula, Oaxaca and Mitla, the Isthmus of Tehuantepec, Morelia, Guadalajara, and Guanajuato. He writes of churches, markets, patios, bull-fights, fiestas, and pilgrimages, and above all of the daily life and beliefs of the Indian villagers. The book has twenty-four plates from his photographs.
